title: metadata-04: require lowercase namespace identifiers
description:
draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-04 requires lowercase namespace identifiers.

-04 §2.1 (registered names): "a sequence of lowercase US-ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores, with no dot (".")."
-04 §2.1 (domain names): "Domain-name identifiers MUST be in lowercase, with internationalized labels in A-label form. Servers MUST reject, with an "invalidProperties" SetError, a /set operation that uses a key that is not a valid namespace identifier, including a domain name containing uppercase ASCII letters."
-04 §8.2.3: "MUST consist of lowercase US-ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores, and MUST NOT contain a dot."
(-02 allowed any-case US-ASCII letters.)

Affected:
- crate-jmap-metadata-types/src/namespace.rs:22-28 is_registered_namespace: uses is_ascii_alphanumeric(), accepts uppercase. Use is_ascii_lowercase() || is_ascii_digit().
- crate-jmap-metadata-types/src/namespace.rs:48-56 is_vendor_namespace: accepts any is_ascii_graphic() byte, including uppercase. Reject uppercase ASCII; an A-label is ASCII, so non-ASCII stays rejected.
- crate-jmap-metadata-types/src/namespace.rs:90 test registered_with_hyphens_underscores_digits asserts "A1-b2_c3" is valid. That oracle was -02; under -04 it must be invalid. Update to the -04 oracle and add uppercase-rejection cases for both kinds (oracle: -04 §2.1 text above).
- crate-jmap-metadata-types/src/capability.rs:43-44 doc ("US-ASCII letters") -> "lowercase".

Effect: is_namespace_supported (crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/validate.rs:106) inherits the stricter check. Function signatures do not change; behavior does (uppercase now rejected).
